source_text: 1. Now enim per alios dispositionem salutis nostree cognovimus, quam per eos per quos Evangelium pervenit ad nos: quod quidem tune preeconayerunt, postea vero per Dei voluntatem in Seripturis nobis tradiderunt, fundamentum et columnam fidei nostree futurum. Nec enim fas est dicere, quoniam ante preedicaverunt quam perfectam haberent agnitionem; sicut quidam audent dicere, gloriantes emendatores se esse Apostolorum. Postea enim quam surrexit Dominus noster a mortuis, et induti sunt supervenientis Spiritus sancti virtutem ex alto, de omnibus adimpleti sunt, et habuerunt perfectam agnitionem; exierunt in fines terree, ea quee a Deo nobis bona sunt evangelizantes, et ccelestem pacem hominibus annuntiantes, qui quidem et omnes pariter et singuli eorum habentes Evangelium Dei*. Ita Mattheus in Hebreis ipsorum lingua scripturam y. edidit Evangelii, cum Petrus et Paulus Rome evangelizarent, et ecxdyoiav. Mera de trav fundarent Ecclesiam. Post vero horum excessum, Marcus discipulus et interpres Petri, et ipse quee a Petro annuntiata erant, per ———— seripta nobis tradidit. Et Lucas autem sectator Pauli, quod ab illo preedicabatur Evangelium, in libro condidit. Postea et Johannes discipulus Domini, qui et supra pectus ejus recumbebat, et ipse edidit Evangelium, Ephesi Asie commorans. Et omnes isti unum Deum factorem cceli et terre a lege et prophetis annuntiatum, et unum Christum filium Dei tradiderunt nobis: quibus si quis non assentit, spernit quidem participes Domini, spernit autem et ipsum Christum Dominum, spernit vero et Patrem, et est a semetipso damnatus, resistens et repugnans saluti suze: quod faciunt omnes heeretici.
pass_a_gloss: Now we have known the disposition of our salvation through others, which through those through whom the Gospel came to us: which indeed they beforehand preached, afterwards however through God's will they handed down to us in Scriptures, the future foundation and column of our faith. For it is not right to say, that they preached before they had perfect knowledge; as certain ones dare to say, boasting themselves to be correctors of the Apostles. For after our Lord rose from the dead, and they were clothed with the power of the Holy Spirit coming from on high, they were filled with all things, and they had perfect knowledge; they went out to the ends of the earth, evangelizing the things that are good for us from God, and announcing heavenly peace to men, who indeed both all equally and each one of them having the Gospel of God. Thus Matthew in the Hebrews' own language published a writing of the Gospel, when Peter and Paul were evangelizing in Rome, and founding the Church. But after the departure of these, Mark, a disciple and interpreter of Peter, and he who had been announced by Peter, handed down to us in writing. And Luke, a follower of Paul, put into a book the Gospel that was being preached by him. Afterwards, John, a disciple of the Lord, who also reclined on His breast, published the Gospel, dwelling in Ephesus of Asia. And all these announced to us one God, the maker of heaven and earth, proclaimed by the law and the prophets, and one Christ, the Son of God: to whom if anyone does not assent, he indeed despises the partakers of the Lord, despises also Christ the Lord, despises also the Father, and is condemned by himself, resisting and opposing his own salvation: which all heretics do.

pass_b_english: We have come to know the plan of our salvation through others — through those, that is, through whom the Gospel reached us. At first the Apostles preached it publicly; later, by God's will, they handed it down to us in the Scriptures, which were to become the foundation and pillar of our faith (1 Timothy 3:15). It is not right to claim that they preached before they possessed full knowledge, as certain people dare to assert, boasting that they are correctors of the Apostles. For after the Lord Jesus rose from the dead, and they were clothed with power from on high when the Holy Spirit came upon them (Luke 24:49; Acts 1:8), they were filled with all things and attained perfect knowledge. They went out to the ends of the earth, proclaiming the good things that come to us from God and announcing heavenly peace to humanity (Luke 2:14; Acts 10:36), each of them equally possessing the Gospel of God. Accordingly, Matthew composed a written Gospel in the Hebrew language while Peter and Paul were evangelizing in Rome and founding the Church. After their departure, Mark, the disciple and interpreter of Peter, handed down in writing what Peter had proclaimed. Luke, a follower of Paul, set down in a book the Gospel that Paul preached. Afterwards, John, the disciple of the Lord who had leaned on His breast (John 13:23), published his Gospel while living in Ephesus in Asia. All these witnesses proclaimed to us one God, the Maker of heaven and earth, announced by the Law and the Prophets, and one Christ, the Son of God. If anyone refuses to assent to them, he despises the Lord's own associates, he despises Christ the Lord, he despises the Father, and he condemns himself by resisting and opposing his own salvation — which is exactly what all heretics do (John 15:23; 1 John 2:22-23).

review.notes: The translation accurately reflects the Latin text. Pass B correctly identifies and adds the necessary scripture citations (1 Timothy 3:15, Luke 24:49, Acts 1:8, Luke 2:14, Acts 10:36, John 13:23, John 15:23, 1 John 2:22-23) which are alluded to in the text but not explicitly written as citations in the Latin source, fulfilling the requirement for added identifications. Pass A is a faithful literal gloss. The title 'Knowledge of Our Salvation' captures the essence of the opening clause.
